translations.literal: In the fifth year, fourth month, he died, aged seventeen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jiande (576), fourth month, he died, aged seventeen.

sentences.zh: 高祖甚痛惜之。

translations.literal: High Ancestor deeply grieved and regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: High Ancestor Yuwen Yong deeply grieved and regretted it.

sentences.zh: 質字乾祐，初封安城公。

translations.literal: Zhi, styled Qianyou, was first enfeoffed as Duke of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, styled Qianyou, was first enfeoffed as Duke of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 後以憲勳，進封河間郡王。

translations.literal: Later, on account of Xian's merit, he was advanced to Prince of Hejian commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on account of Yuwen Xian's merit, he was advanced to Prince of Hejian commandery.

sentences.zh: 賨字乾禮，大將軍、中垻公。

translations.literal: Cong, styled Qianli, was grand general and Duke of Zhongao.
translations.idiomatic: Cong, styled Qianli, was grand general and Duke of Zhongao.

sentences.zh: 貢出後莒莊公。

translations.literal: Gong was adopted out to Duke Zhuang of Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Gong was adopted out to Duke Zhuang of Ju.

sentences.zh: 乾禧，安城公。

translations.literal: Qianxi was Duke of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qianxi was Duke of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 乾洽，龍涸公。

translations.literal: Qianqia was Duke of Longhu.
translations.idiomatic: Qianqia was Duke of Longhu.

sentences.zh: 並與憲俱被誅。

translations.literal: All were executed together with Xian.
translations.idiomatic: All were executed together with Yuwen Xian.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：自兩漢逮乎魏、晉，其帝弟帝子衆矣，唯楚元、河間、東平、陳思之徒以文儒播美，任城、琅邪以武功馳譽。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: From the Two Han through Wei and Jin, imperial younger brothers and imperial sons were many; only Prince Yuan of Chu, Prince of Hejian, Prince of Dongping, Prince Si of Chen, and the like spread fame through literary learning; Prince of Rencheng and Prince of Langye won renown through martial achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: From the Two Han through Wei and Jin, imperial younger brothers and imperial sons were many; only Prince Yuan of Chu, Prince of Hejian, Prince of Dongping, Prince Si of Chen, and the like spread fame through literary learning; Prince of Rencheng and Prince of Langye won renown through martial achievement.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 體自尊極，長於宮闈，佚樂侈其心，驕貴蕩其志，故使奇才高行，終鮮于天下之士焉。

translations.literal: In status they were most exalted; raised long in palace quarters—idleness and pleasure unsettled their hearts, pride and privilege dissipated their wills—so that men of unusual talent and lofty conduct were in the end rarely found among gentlemen of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In status they were most exalted; raised long in palace quarters—idleness and pleasure unsettled their hearts, pride and privilege dissipated their wills—so that men of unusual talent and lofty conduct were in the end rarely found among gentlemen of the realm.

sentences.zh: 齊王奇姿傑出，獨牢籠於前載。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi was singularly outstanding in wondrous stature, alone unmatched in past ages.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian was singularly outstanding in wondrous stature, alone unmatched in past ages.

sentences.zh: 以介弟之地，居上將之重，智勇冠世，攻戰如神，敵國繫以存亡，鼎命由其輕重。

translations.literal: With the standing of a younger brother by birth, he bore the weight of a commander-in-chief; wisdom and courage topped his age; in attack and battle he was like a spirit—the survival of enemy states hung on him; the destiny of the realm turned on his rise and fall.
translations.idiomatic: With the standing of a younger brother by birth, he bore the weight of a commander-in-chief; wisdom and courage topped his age; in attack and battle he was like a spirit—the survival of enemy states hung on him; the destiny of the realm turned on his rise and fall.

sentences.zh: 比之異姓，則方、召、韓、白，何以加茲。

translations.literal: Compared with men of other surnames—Fang and Shao, Han and Bai—how could they surpass this?
translations.idiomatic: Compared with men of other surnames—Fang Shu and the Duke of Shao, Han Xin and Bai Qi—how could they surpass this?

sentences.zh: 挾震主之威，屬道消之日，斯人而嬰斯戮，君子是以知周祚之不永也。

translations.literal: Clutching the awe that overawes his master, at a time when the Way was waning—such a man yet met such punishment—the gentleman therefore knows that Zhou's fortune would not long endure.
translations.idiomatic: Clutching the awe that overawes his master, at a time when the Way was waning—such a man yet met such punishment—the gentleman therefore knows that Zhou's fortune would not long endure.

sentences.zh: 昔張耳、陳餘賓客厮役，所居皆取卿相。

translations.literal: Formerly Zhang Er and Chen Yu's guests and servants—those they employed all rose to minister and commandant rank.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Zhang Er and Chen Yu's guests and servants—those they employed all rose to minister and commandant rank.

sentences.zh: 而齊之文武僚吏，其後亦多至台牧。

translations.literal: Yet the Prince of Qi's civil and military staff—afterward also mostly reached high provincial posts.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yuwen Xian's civil and military staff—afterward also mostly reached high provincial posts.

sentences.zh: 異世同符，可謂賢矣。

translations.literal: Different ages, same tally—one may call them worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Different ages, same tally—one may call them worthy.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text uses the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the 《Book of Zhou》, November 1971, as the base for collation.
translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the 《Book of Zhou》 (November 1971).
